title: Playing the Ziegfeld Follies and the Cotton Club for $125 a week
summary: He played the Follies from eight, then raced by taxi to the Cotton Club until three, for $125 a week, unsure whether there was a night off.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: So I joined the band, and we used to play in the Zigfield show at night, and after the show, we would get in two taxicabs and run right over to the Cotton Club and play over there -- and we'd play at the Cotton Club until three o'clock. We had two shows, and he gave me $125 a week, which was a lot of money at that particular time, for playing both at the Zigfield Follies and at the Cotton Club.
So what time did the show start at the Zigfield Follies?
Well, it was regular legit show, like eight o'clock or eight thirty, or something like that.
What time were you through at the Cotton Club?
At the Cotton Club? Three o'clock.
And you worked from eight to three every night?
Oh, yes indeed. No, we used to be -- we didn't have a night off in New York, huh?
You didn't have a night off?
I can't remember if we got a night off. I think so, it must be -- because in New York there was a law to have a night off somewhere, you know?
I thiknk we had a night off, but I just don't quite remember -- that was a long time ago.
